newsitem.title: USA: NY police raid apartment, seize explosive devices.
newsitem.headline: NY police raid apartment, seize explosive devices.

text.p: Police made a daring raid on a New York apartment on Thursday, seizing several pipe bombs and arresting three "Middle Eastern" men suspected of making explosive devices, officials said.

New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said the Joint Terrorism Task Force of local, state and federal agencies was investigating whether there was a possible plot to bomb New York subways or other targets.
"That's one of the things being looked at," Giuliani told WCBS Radio in an interview. "The subways were closed down because the building is essentially right over a station.
"One of things being looked at it is, was there a plan to bomb various subway stations and if there was one, was it a realistic one," the mayor said.

Two of those arrested were shot by police officers who said they saw them lunge for one of the possible explosive devices as the early morning raid was in progress, officials said. The lives of the wounded men were not in danger and they were in custody in a hospital.

Four or five cylindrical pipe bombs were found in the ramshackle apartment in the Park Slope residential neighbourhood of Brooklyn, police sources said. City and federal officials declined to comment on the specific nature of the devices.

"We don't know exactly what this is at this point, but obviously the investigation is continuing," James Kallstrom, the head of New York's FBI office told a news conference at City Hall. "There are a lot of leads, we're not going to talk about those."

Police ordered the raid after receiving a tip by telephone at 10:45 p.m. EDT on Wednesday (0245 GMT Thursday), officials said. Police entered the apartment at 4:40 a.m. EDT Thursday (0840 GMT) and found three men sleeping inside and the suspicious devices.
"The individuals involved are Middle Eastern but we don't have definite confirmation of their nations of origin yet," the mayor told reporters.

Agents from the New York bomb squad, the FBI, Joint Terrorism Task Force and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms cordoned off a four-block wide area around the apartment, evacuated residents and diverted subway services.
The raid created chaos for residents in the neighbourhood as police awoke them in the early hours. About 90 people were evacuated from their homes.

"I was sleeping and they were banging on the doors," said resident Evita Carabello, who lives in an apartment building near the one that was raided. "They were yelling and yelling 'you have to leave, leave the house now because there's a bomb'."
Four subway lines were diverted by the investigation, leaving hundreds of thousands of commuters seeking alternative transport.
